correctness.rationale: Independent thinning of vertex Poisson calls yields independent bidirectional contact processes on each undirected edge at rates 1/deg(x)+1/deg(y). Accordingly T^(a)=max(M_a,E+M_b), with independent E~Exp(1/(a+1)+1/(b+1)), M_a and M_b maxima of Exp(1+1/(a+1)), Exp(1+1/(b+1)) leaf clocks. Conditioning on E proves displayed CDF and finite Laplace-binomial moments. The ratio F_Ma/F_Mb is nondecreasing since a>=b, r_a<=r_b and r/expm1(rt) decreases in r; independent direct derivative evaluations confirm its sign at tested sizes. The ratio lemma then yields uniform deadline stochastic order. For b/log a->rho>0, maxima M_a/log a->1, M_b/log a->0 and E/log a->rho Exp(1), yielding the limiting atom and finishing side by a boundary-continuity argument; exponential-max Gumbel laws cover b=o(log a) and b/log a->infinity with b=o(a). Bounds on second moments give the mean limits. Finite Markov checks in package inspected only; not treated as general proof.

value.rationale: Double stars are canonical two-community bottlenecks for rumor spreading. The source stochastic order at every deadline and critical atom tracking which community finishes last identify actionable finite-time mechanisms distinct from merely first-order broadcast time growth. The b~log a threshold is motivated by comparison of bridge waiting time b and a-side extreme leaf waiting log a.
